scenes.text: An AI agent can trade for you. The hard part is trusting it.
Give it the keys, and one bad answer can empty the vault. Afterwards, all you have is its word for why it traded.
Autonr splits the job in three. The agent decides whether to trade. Chainlink and Supra decide the price. And a vault on Hedera enforces both, before a single token moves.
scenes.say: Autoner splits the job in three. The agent decides whether to trade. Chainlink and Supra decide the price. And a vault on Hedera enforces both, before a single token moves.

scenes.text: Before every trade, the agent writes down why. It publishes that reasoning to a Hedera Consensus Service topic first. Only its own key can write there.

Then it asks the vault to trade, and cites that message: its hash, and its number. The vault reads both oracles itself, checks its limits, and sets the minimum it will accept. The agent never names a price.
On testnet, the vault sold five dollars of HBAR on SaucerSwap. Trade number eight.
scenes.say: On testnet, the vault sold five dollars of H-bar on SaucerSwap. Trade number eight.

scenes.text: Anyone can check it, from public data alone. Twelve checks. The message matches its hash. It reached consensus four seconds before the trade. One key signed both.
Change one letter of the reasoning, and the proof fails.
Now ask the vault to break its own rules. Too large. Wrong token. Wrong pool. No reasoning. Old reasoning. Wrong caller. Six requests, six refusals.
The testnet pool prices HBAR nearly twenty times above the market. Sells pass. Buys are refused, because the oracles say no.
scenes.say: The testnet pool prices H-bar nearly twenty times above the market. Sells pass. Buys are refused, because the oracles say no.

scenes.text: And the log has no gaps. Every trade traces back to exactly one decision, published first.
The Consensus Service holds the reasoning. A smart contract enforces the policy. The Token Service moves the funds. And any agent built with the Hedera Agent Kit can trade this way.
